passages.note: House Third Reading roll call on a single-subject gestational-limit bill; 26 of 60 voted No, so it is not near-unanimous.
passages.actor_quote: DEGRAZIA N DIAZ Y DUNN Y

passages.provision_quote: Except in a medical emergency, a physician may not intentionally or knowingly perform, induce or attempt to perform or induce an abortion if the probable gestational age of the unborn human being has been determined to be greater than fifteen weeks.
passages.note: The enacted text sets the limit at fifteen weeks, which falls between the first-trimester rung and the second-trimester rung and matches neither one's time clause.
Overview page lists him among the co-sponsors; only one Diaz appears, and the page prints no first name or initial.

rows.reasoning: Diaz co-sponsored SB 1164 (2022) and voted Aye on House Third Reading; the enacted text provides that "a physician may not intentionally or knowingly perform, induce or attempt to perform or induce an abortion if the probable gestational age of the unborn human being has been determined to be greater than fifteen weeks", except in a medical emergency. A fifteen-week limit still permits elective abortion past the first trimester, so it does not match "allow abortion during the first trimester, and after that only to protect the mother's health", and it bans most of the second trimester, so it does not match "keep abortion legal through the second trimester, and after that only to protect the mother's health". The record places him on the restricting side without matching the clauses of any one rung, and naming the nearest rung by elimination would be the tiebreaker the codebook forbids.
